summary: This work demonstrates pulse-level quantum state preparation in transmon qubits by directly optimizing entanglement measures rather than targeting specific states, achieving Bell states with negativity $\mathcal{N}(\rho_{01}) \approx 0.499$, GHZ states with three-tangle $\tau_3 \approx 0.999$, and W states with balanced squared concurrences $\mathcal{C}^2(\rho_{ij}) \approx 0.44$ on the IBM Sherbrooke architecture. The resource-oriented approach yields substantially shorter pulse sequences—1379 dt for Bell, 3750 dt for GHZ, and 6132 dt for W states—compared to transpiled gate-based circuits (2912 dt, 5315 dt, and 8224 dt respectively), with reduced expressivity that naturally suppresses barren plateaus in variational algorithms.
motivation: Near-term superconducting quantum processors suffer from decoherence and gate infidelities; designing shorter state-preparation protocols that minimize total evolution time while reducing effective expressivity could mitigate these errors and improve trainability of variational circuits by suppressing barren plateau phenomena.
method: Differential evolution optimization of piecewise-constant and Gaussian-square envelope functions on drive channels (D0, D1, D2) and cross-resonance control channels (U0, U1) of three transmon qubits coupled linearly with $J_{01} \approx 0.013$ GHz and $J_{12} \approx 0.014$ GHz; cost functions target entanglement measures (negativity, three-tangle, concurrence) rather than specific target states, with integration via jax_odeint in qiskit_dynamics using hardware parameters from Fake_Sherbrooke.
result: Two-qubit Bell-like states achieve maximal negativity at 0.499 within 1379 dt; three-qubit GHZ states reach three-tangle 0.999 in 3750 dt; W states achieve squared concurrences near 4/9 (≈0.444) in 6132 dt and pass Bures-distance validation ($D_B = 1.3 \times 10^{-5}$ from ideal W), all substantially faster than gate-decomposed circuits while maintaining quality in three-level transmon models.
